about:
devtools/measure.sh kblock-rolled-compile [--backend cuda|hip]   a compiler
    devtools/measure.sh kblock-rolled [--backend cuda|hip]           timed

declared.hypothesis: E read from global memory and the contraction as loops make every l <= 3 K class compile in minutes; the loops cost (dd|dd) wall-clock against the unrolled kb, which keeps its compile-time constant indices
declared.rule: per arch: the median over the timed runs of the (dd|dd) class's events, rolled / kb: 'faster' below 0.95, 'slower' above 1.05, else 'neutral'. A RECORD, not a gate (#571): kb stays the default through d whatever it reads
declared.expected: slower: the rolled stages read E and the tables from global memory and R from local memory per term

kb_ff_not_compiled.nvcc: killed in cicc at 2.8 h, 2.28 GB RSS (E composed); 2.7 h, 2.26 GB (E factored)

terms.S: a kernel's sum over KB_PROFILE_STALLS of smsp__average_warps_issue_stalled_<r>_per_issue_active.ratio: cycles between a warp's issues, by reason
terms.hot: kbr's share of PC samples on the source lines that read Ebd[ (stage 1) or Eac[ (stage 2): the rolled loops

H1.hypothesis: kbr is latency-bound on dependent loads in its inner loops
H1.supported: mem(kbr) >= 0.5, long_scoreboard kbr's largest stall reason, and hot(kbr) >= 0.5

H2.hypothesis: kb's spills mostly hit L1, or sit outside the hot region
H2.supported: hit(kb) >= 0.8, or long(kb) <= 0.25 (local traffic, whatever its hit rate, does not stall kb)

H3.hypothesis: the unrolled text gives the scheduler parallelism that a CSR row loop does not
H3.supported: warps(kb) <= 1.1 warps(kbr) (no more warps to hide latency with) and issue(kb) >= 1.5 issue(kbr): kb's extra issue is per-warp parallelism

profile_declared.card: RTX 3080 (sm_86) only: the RX 9060 XT has no fp64 or byte counters (measured_store.UNMEASURED, #140)

dense_declared.hypothesis: with the (a,c) and (b,d) rows rolled and p, q unrolled over dense E, every p + q is a compile-time constant: the R array, the hpq / bd_q / ac_p indirection and #574's dependent bd_q -> hpq -> R load chain are gone, at the price of the structural zeros' multiplies; the text grows as n_p n_q, not n_ac n_bd n_p n_q, so (ff|ff) compiles
dense_declared.rule: per arch and class: the median over the timed runs of the class's events, dense / other for each other arm timed beside it (kb and rolled at (dd|dd), rolled at (ff|ff)): 'faster' below 0.95, 'slower' above 1.05, else 'neutral'. The form a class should use is the fastest arm that compiles, read from these medians; a RECORD, not a gate
dense_declared.expected: (dd|dd): dense faster than rolled, slower than kb; (ff|ff): dense faster than rolled
